name: @apex-inc/mcp-server

tools.name: plan_experiment
tools.description: Apex — PLANNING ONLY, does not create anything. Analyzes a goal against existing beliefs and experiments, then returns structured options for the user to choose from. After calling, you MUST present the returned options as a numbered list or poll and wait for the user to pick before calling any other Apex tools.

goal.description: What the user wants to improve or test (e.g. 'improve signup conversion on landing page')

target_url.description: URL of the page to test, if known

tools.name: start_reasoning
tools.description: Apex — Record a belief and hypothesis chain. Only call AFTER the user has picked a belief statement and confidence level from the options you presented.

decision.description: What you want to improve or change

belief.description: The assumption — must be confirmed by the user

confidence.description: How sure the user is about this assumption (0-100%) — must be chosen by the user

tools.name: create_belief
tools.description: Apex — Record an assumption your team is making. Confirm the belief statement and confidence with the user before calling.

parent_belief_id.description: ID of a parent assumption, if this is a sub-assumption

tools.name: create_experiment
tools.description: Apex — Create an experiment record. Returns a structured recipe for the AI agent to implement. The agent makes the actual code changes using useApexVariant hook — Apex never generates code. Always call with preview=true first so the user sees a summary.

target_url.description: URL of the page to test on the ACTIVE workspace (include #anchor for section targeting). Must be a host this workspace has actually sent events from — never guess a brand domain or a sibling workspace's site. Required for web and mobile; not used for surface 'paid_channel'.

control_content.description: The current content that the control shows. Required for web and mobile; not used for surface 'paid_channel'.

variant_content.description: The new content for the variant. Required for web and mobile; not used for surface 'paid_channel'.

target_component.description: Component or file path where the change should be made

belief_id.description: ID of the assumption this tests

belief_statement.description: If you don't have a beliefId, pass the assumption statement and Apex will create the belief (and a hypothesis) and link them to this experiment.

belief_confidence.description: Confidence (0-100%) for the belief created from beliefStatement. Defaults to 50.

hypothesis_statement.description: Optional hypothesis statement to record alongside a belief created from beliefStatement.

primary_metric_event.description: Canonical event name the experiment optimizes, e.g. 'add_to_cart', 'checkout_completed', 'form_submit'. Validated against the workspace event spec. Prefer an OUTCOME event (purchase/signup) over a proxy (email_open) — use list_metrics to see which are DETECTED with volume.

primary_metric_type.description: How the goal is measured. 'rate' (default) = did it happen. 'revenue'/'duration' = a continuous value summed per subject (set primaryMetricValueProperty). Use 'revenue' for Stripe/purchase-value goals.

primary_metric_value_property.description: For revenue/duration goals: the event property to sum, e.g. 'value'. Defaults to 'value'.

guardrail_event.description: Canonical protective event for an EXTRA guardrail that must not regress (e.g. 'purchase_refunded', 'app_uninstall', 'js_error'). Apex already auto-protects revenue/refunds/errors by default — only pass this to add a test-specific harm signal. Use list_metrics({role:'guardrail'}) to see what's firing. Choose one ORTHOGONAL to the primary goal.

guardrail_type.description: How the guardrail is measured. 'rate' (default) = how often the harm event fires. 'revenue' = sum a value (e.g. refund $).

guardrail_threshold.description: Harm margin for the guardrail, RELATIVE (0.25 = flag a >25% rise). Defaults to 0.25.

prediction_magnitude.description: Your committed prediction of the effect, e.g. '10% lift'. Recorded with 'agent' provenance and used for calibration. Required before the experiment can be ACTIVATED.

surface.description: The PROPERTY the experiment runs in (not the SDK used): 'web' for a website, 'mobile' for a native / Capacitor / React-Native app, 'paid_channel' for an Ad holdout (Apex holds a share of known people back from the workspace's ads on one network and measures the installs the ads actually caused — pass paid_channel too). OPTIONAL for web/mobile — when omitted it is auto-detected from repo signals (capacitor.config.* / @apex-inc/capacitor-plugin → mobile) and the workspace's registered data sources; pass it explicitly only to override or when both web and mobile sources exist. Sets the dashboard data-source label (Website vs Mobile app vs Ads).

network.description: Ad network the ad sets run on. Apex attaches the do-not-show list itself on Meta only; other networks are manual attach.

ad_account_id.description: The connected ad account the ad sets belong to. Omit to use the account the workspace connected for this network.

ad_set_ids.description: Ad set ids to hold people back from (max 20). Frozen at create; changing them is a new holdout.

holdout_percent.description: Share of the known population held back, 0.05–0.5 (0.2 = one in five).

attach_mode.description: 'apex' = Apex puts the list on the ad sets and checks daily (Meta only). 'manual' = the owner adds the audience as an exclusion by hand; Apex checks daily and counts nothing until it is on. Defaults to 'apex' on Meta, 'manual' elsewhere.

washout_days.description: Days after the list lands before installs count, so pre-list ad exposure washes out. Default 3.

population_segment_id.description: Optional Segment id narrowing who can be drawn.

paid_channel.description: Ad holdout settings. Required when surface is 'paid_channel'; rejected otherwise. The primary metric is always app installs, so primaryMetricEvent is not needed.

data_source_id.description: Optional explicit Data Source (property) id this experiment runs in, e.g. 'ds_website' or 'ds_ios'. Usually inferred from surface; pass it to bind to a specific registered source. Tenant-validated server-side.

randomization_unit.description: What to bucket on. Default 'visitor' (per-device). Use 'person' to give one stitched user the same variant across their devices, or 'account'/'org' for B2B account-level tests where everyone in an account should see the same variant.

min_sample_per_arm.description: Minimum exposed subjects PER ARM before a winner can be claimed (the sample gate). Defaults to 50. Raise it to demand more evidence (detect a smaller lift); lower it (floor 30) for low-traffic properties that would otherwise stall. The real winner-gate is still the 95% probability-to-be-best — this only sets the traffic floor. Pre-registration: frozen once the experiment is running.

runtime_days.description: How long to run the experiment, in days (the decision window). Apex force-concludes at this point — decisive winner if reached, else inconclusive. Defaults to 14. Set e.g. 28 to run for four weeks. This is the max runtime, not a minimum: a decisive winner can conclude sooner. Pre-registration: frozen once the experiment is running (fork to change it).

preview.description: If true, returns a preview without creating. Default: true.

tools.name: attach_experiment_asset
tools.description: Apex — Attach a variant screenshot to an experiment. Use after capturing a control/variant screenshot: for localhost or auth-gated pages the agent captures, pass imageBase64; for an already-hosted image, pass url. The stored asset shows on the dashboard experiment card and the experiment detail gallery.

experiment_id.description: The experiment ID to attach the screenshot to

image_base64.description: Base64-encoded PNG/JPEG. For localhost/auth-gated pages captured by the agent.

viewport.description: Viewport the screenshot was captured at (default desktop).

commit_sha.description: Optional commit SHA the screenshot corresponds to.

tools.name: recapture_experiment_screenshots
tools.description: Apex — Re-run the hosted screenshot capture for a WEB experiment's arms (renders the target URL for control + variant and stores the images shown on the dashboard). Use after the variant is deployed. For unpublished SDK / Cursor drafts, attach localhost shots with attach_experiment_asset instead — hosted recapture of a public URL will be refused.

experiment_id.description: The experiment ID to re-capture screenshots for.

tools.name: verify_experiment_wiring
tools.description: Apex — Verify an experiment is actually wired up before launch: check whether `experiment_exposure` events are arriving for BOTH arms. Use this before activate_experiment to avoid launching an experiment that silently collects no data. Returns a per-arm exposure breakdown and an actionable next step.

experiment_id.description: The experiment ID to verify wiring for

tools.name: activate_experiment
tools.description: Apex — Launch an experiment. Changes its status from draft to running. Traffic will be split immediately. Before flipping to running, this verifies BOTH arms are producing `experiment_exposure` events (wiring check). Code-wired (SDK-hook) experiments may be activated before their code ships: the server holds them in `pending_deployment` ("Waiting on deploy") and starts on the first exposure. Snippet experiments and journey_arm message tests do not need pre-activation exposures — journey traffic starts on the next send once running. Only wired web experiments that genuinely can't self-start are refused unless force is true. Ask the user to confirm before calling.

force.description: Override the wiring safety check and activate even if both arms aren't producing exposures yet. Use only when you knowingly accept launching without verified wiring.

tools.name: pause_experiment
tools.description: Apex — Pause a running experiment. All visitors will see the control until resumed. Ask the user to confirm before calling.

tools.name: track_deployment
tools.description: Apex — Record that an experiment's code has been committed and pushed. Stores the commit SHA and monitors deployment status. Call after pushing the experiment code.

commit_sha.description: The git commit SHA containing the experiment code

tools.name: check_deployment
tools.description: Apex — Check if an experiment's code has been deployed. Verifies that the assignment endpoint responds for this experiment. Call after track_deployment.

tools.name: archive_experiment
tools.description: Apex — Archive an experiment. Removes it from active views but preserves all data, learnings, and belief graph connections. Archived experiments still contribute to intelligence scoring and recommendations. A RUNNING experiment cannot be archived — end it first (conclude_experiment / promote_winner) so its result + belief are captured; the server returns 409 archive_requires_conclusion otherwise. Ask the user to confirm before calling.

tools.name: list_experiments
tools.description: Apex — List the user's Apex experiments. Call this ONLY when the user explicitly asks about their experiments or what's running/ready to graduate. Do not call it proactively for unrelated tasks. Archived experiments are hidden by default — pass status "archived" to see them, or "all" to see everything. Experiments that are promoted but not graduated are flagged as PENDING GRADUATION.

status.description: Filter by status. Defaults to showing all except archived.

tools.name: get_results
tools.description: Apex — Get the website experiment card: visitors, conversions, and confidence from GET /api/experiments/:id?unified=true. For readiness (collecting / decisive / inconclusive) or a letter Experiment step, use get_experiment_results.

tools.name: list_beliefs
tools.description: Apex — List the workspace's beliefs (the assumptions experiments test). Shows confidence, validation state, and AI-generated provenance so you can LINK an existing belief instead of minting a duplicate.

query.description: Filter beliefs by a keyword in the statement

tools.name: list_belief_suggestions
tools.description: Apex — "Worth writing down": settled experiments whose verdict passes the belief gate (decisive, exclusion attached the whole window for Ad holdouts, no sample-ratio mismatch, no guardrail breach, both arms over the events floor) and have not been written down as a belief yet. Statistical only; no model in the path. Pass experimentId for one experiment and, when nothing is offered, 'blocker' says why in one word. Each row carries the sentence Apex would write and the evidence line; write one down with accept_belief_suggestion.

experiment_id.description: One experiment. Omit for the workspace's rail (newest settled first).

tools.name: accept_belief_suggestion
tools.description: Apex — Write a settled experiment's verdict down as one belief. Creates the Belief with the experiment as its supporting evidence and generatedFromExperimentId set; its evidence state starts at 'one study' and moves to 'validated' when a second test agrees. 'statement' is the workspace's edit of the sentence (the numbers and evidence line stay Apex's). The gate re-runs here, so an experiment list_belief_suggestions would not offer is refused with its blocker. Writing it twice returns the existing belief. Admin only.

experiment_id.description: The settled experiment to write down.

statement.description: The owner's wording of the belief. Omit to accept Apex's sentence as written.

tools.name: verify_ad_exclusion
tools.description: Apex — Ad holdout only (surface paid_channel). Ask Apex to check, right now, whether the do-not-show list is on every ad set the holdout covers, and record the answer. Nothing is counted until this reads "attached"; the daily check runs on its own, so call this after the list lands or after the workspace attached it by hand. Rate-limited: a recent check returns the last reading instead of re-reading.

tools.name: attach_ad_exclusion
tools.description: Apex — Ad holdout only (surface paid_channel, Meta only). Apex puts the held-back list on the holdout's ad sets itself: exactly one exclusion added per ad set, every other targeting key (locations, age, placements, ...) left as read, then read back to confirm. Two steps, always in this order: (1) call with preview=true (default) and SHOW the workspace the before/after per ad set — which ad sets get the exclusion, which already have it, which are on another account and will not be touched; (2) once the workspace confirms, call with preview=false. The first real attach in a workspace needs acknowledge=true, which records the workspace's standing allowance for Apex to edit ad-set targeting (say so before passing it; never pass it without the workspace having seen the preview). Refuses with needs_targeting_ack when it is missing, list_not_on_network while the list is still syncing, and not for Google/TikTok/LinkedIn (there the owner adds the list in the network's tools and verify_ad_exclusion checks). Ending, pausing or archiving the holdout takes the list off again on its own. Not billed.

preview.description: true (default): read-only — return the before/after per ad set and whether the allowance is on file. false: make the edit.

acknowledge.description: Pass true on the first real attach in this workspace, after the owner has seen the preview and agreed that Apex may edit ad-set targeting. Recorded once per network.

tools.name: detach_ad_exclusion
tools.description: Apex — Ad holdout only (surface paid_channel, Meta only). Take Apex's exclusion back off the holdout's ad sets and delete the held-back list from Meta. Removes only what Apex added: a list the owner attached by hand is refused (not_apex_attached) and the owner removes it in Ads Manager. Ending, pausing or archiving the holdout does this on its own; call this only to undo an attach early. Admin only. Confirm with the workspace first: the held-back people start seeing the ads again and the holdout stops measuring.

tools.name: update_experiment
tools.description: Apex — Edit an EXISTING experiment. Editability is gated by lifecycle: a DRAFT (with no exposures yet) is fully editable; once it has data or is running, the pre-registration (hypothesis, metric, guardrails) and bucketing (surface, variants) freeze and edits return a clear "experiment_locked" reason. After freeze, fork_experiment instead. Use this to fix a mislabeled surface or correct a draft before launch.

surface.description: Correct the surface — editable only on a draft with 0 exposures (web↔mobile). 'paid_channel' is accepted only when the draft already carries its Ad holdout block.

target_url.description: Retarget a DRAFT to a URL on the ACTIVE workspace. Same host rules as create_experiment.

prediction_id.description: Attach a minted prediction id (from log_prediction) to this draft. Also stamps the prediction onto the experiment's hypothesis when that link is missing. Required before activation.

primary_metric_event.description: Change the primary metric's canonical event — draft only.

guardrail_event.description: Replace the guardrail with this canonical protective event — draft only.

min_sample_per_arm.description: Set the minimum exposed subjects PER ARM before a winner can be claimed (the sample gate; floor 30). Draft only — it's part of the pre-registration and freezes at launch (a running experiment returns experiment_locked; fork to change it).

runtime_days.description: Set how long to run the experiment, in days (the decision window Apex force-concludes at). Draft only — part of the pre-registration; freezes at launch (fork to change it).

tools.name: fork_experiment
tools.description: Apex — Duplicate a frozen experiment's design into a fresh editable DRAFT. Use this after update_experiment reports "experiment_locked" (running or has exposures). The fork carries NO data (no results, assignments, or winner) and records its lineage; edit it freely, then activate.

tools.name: check_experiment_conflicts
tools.description: Apex — Before you create or activate an experiment, check who else is live on that page. Pin a part (target_anchor) so two homepage experiments are not the same place. Whole page plus a part is one place. Different named parts: the same person can see both — say so, do not add the two lifts. Overlap: Someone could see both; Keep them apart with set_experiment_mutex, or wait. Shared conversion on the allowed mix: one experiment or wait. Pass either experimentId OR the candidate's location + primaryMetricEvent. Advisory only.

experiment_id.description: Check an existing experiment by id (loads its location + metric).

tools.name: check_live_tests
tools.description: Apex — Before you edit a page, commit, or push, call this even if the user did not mention experiments. Also call it before you change a letter, Adaptive Journey, or Milestone. If something live is on those files or ids, stop and ask. Do not edit. Do not commit.

file_paths.description: Repo-relative paths you are about to edit or commit. Full file is read locally when content is omitted.

content.description: Full file at HEAD, not the diff hunk.

urls.description: Page URLs you are about to change. URL-only hits are a warning, not a stop.

communication_ids.description: Letters you are about to edit or publish.

journey_ids.description: Adaptive Journeys you are about to change or publish.

milestone_ids.description: Milestones you are about to change or delete.

tools.name: set_experiment_mutex
tools.description: Apex — Put two experiments in a mutual-exclusion group: no visitor is ever assigned to both, so they run concurrently with partitioned traffic (the scientifically clean way to run two experiments that touch the same surface). Bidirectional. Pass mode:"remove" to unlink. Safe on running experiments — only affects future assignments.

with_experiment_id.description: The other experiment to make mutually exclusive with.

tools.name: suggest_experiment
tools.description: Apex — Get smart experiment suggestions based on context. Analyzes your assumptions, past experiments, and confidence gaps to recommend what to test next.

context.description: What you're working on (e.g. 'redesigning onboarding', 'pricing page optimization')

tools.name: promote_winner
tools.description: Apex — Promote the winner on a website experiment card (PATCH /api/experiments action=promote). The snippet serves that arm immediately. For a letter Experiment step, use promote_experiment_winner. After promoting, use graduate_experiment to put the winner in source.

tools.name: get_experiment_results
tools.description: Apex — Readiness + results for a letter Experiment step (or any experiment): collecting / decisive / inconclusive / guardrail from GET /api/experiments/:id/results. For the website experiment card (visitors and conversions), use get_results.

tools.name: promote_experiment_winner
tools.description: Apex — Promote the winner of a letter Experiment step (or any unified experiment). Re-verifies the readiness gate server-side and writes the winning variant's content into the canonical communication as a new version; losing variants are archived. For the website experiment card, use promote_winner. Pass force=true to override "not enough people yet." Force cannot override a page that changed mid-flight.

force.description: Override the readiness gate and promote anyway

winner_key.description: Explicit winner variant key (defaults to the decisive winner)

tools.name: graduate_experiment
tools.description: Apex — Get instructions to make a promoted experiment's winning changes permanent in the codebase. Returns the original values (for searching in source files) and new values (for replacement). After making the edits and deploying, the Apex snippet automatically detects the native changes and marks the experiment as graduated.

tools.name: record_outcome
tools.description: Apex — Log the outcome of an experiment and update belief confidence. Present the outcome interpretation to the user and let them confirm before recording.

tools.name: predict_impact
tools.description: Apex — Decision guardrail: predict the impact of a proposed change by searching history for similar experiments. Returns historical data, confidence, and a recommendation.

description.description: Description of the proposed change (e.g. 'increase signup form fields from 3 to 5')

tools.name: evaluate_feature
tools.description: Apex — Pre-build decision intelligence: evaluate a feature idea against the belief graph, past experiments, and intelligence score before committing to building it.

feature.description: Description of the feature you're considering building

target_metric.description: The metric you expect this feature to improve (e.g. 'conversion_rate', 'activation')

tools.name: link_experiment
tools.description: Apex — Link an experiment to a GitHub pull request or issue. The link is what auto-starts the experiment when the PR merges. The convention "apex/exp_XXX" in your PR title also auto-links, but call this explicitly to be sure.

system.description: Which dev tool the work item lives in (github for PRs)

url.description: Canonical URL of the work item

tools.name: unlink_experiment
tools.description: Apex — Remove an Engineering Link from an experiment.

tools.name: gate_experiment_on_merge
tools.description: Apex — Arm a merge gate: bind an experiment to a linked PR so merging it auto-starts the test. Requires a frozen design spec (primary metric, minimum sample size, max duration, stopping rule) — this is the rigor gate that stops PR latency from changing the rules of the test. Link the PR first with link_experiment.

engineering_link_id.description: The link id of the PR (from list_engineering_links)

ramp_on_merge.description: Variant traffic split applied on merge (default 50)

primary_metric.description: Primary metric key (must be one of the experiment's metrics)

min_sample_size.description: Minimum per-variant sample size (must exceed the default 10)

tools.name: open_graduation_pr
tools.description: Apex — Open an Apex-authored Graduation PR that inlines the winning variant in the merchant's repo. Requires the repo to be opted in for Apex writes (Automation Controls). The experiment must be promoted with a winner. No LLM — a deterministic, reviewable manifest + branded PR.

experiment_id.description: The experiment ID (must be promoted with a winner)

tools.name: open_revert_pr
tools.description: Apex — Open a native-format Revert PR removing a losing experiment's variant. Requires the repo to be opted in for Apex writes.

tools.name: get_automation_controls
tools.description: Apex — Read the workspace's Graduation Pipeline Automation Controls (on-conclusion behavior, per-repo write allowlist, GitHub visibility, commit/branch conventions).

tools.name: update_automation_controls
tools.description: Apex — Update the workspace's Graduation Pipeline Automation Controls. Only the fields you pass change. To let Apex open PRs to a repo, add it via writeRepos (or use the dedicated repos endpoint).

tools.name: list_engineering_links
tools.description: Apex — List the PRs and issues linked to an experiment, with their current state.

tools.name: recommend_communications
tools.description: Get recommended lifecycle communications for your vertical and conversion model. Returns a prioritized list of emails and push notifications to set up.

tools.name: generate_communications
tools.description: Create your communication program from recommendations. Pass catalog entry IDs to generate tenant communications with pre-written copy. Each new letter wears the workspace default Theme (Title / Body / Button look is snapshotted; catalog copy is not rewritten to match). Preview with preview_communication to see theme roles vs block overrides.

catalog_entry_ids.description: IDs from the recommendation output to generate

tools.name: list_communications
tools.description:
List the workspace's communication templates (email / inbox / web push / mobile push) with the fields you need to CHOOSE one — for a journey send step, a broadcast, or a transactional send. Returns per template: title, version, status, pipeline, channels, subject, a one-line body preview so you can disambiguate similar titles without opening each one, and controlState. Pipeline is 'transactional' (bypasses opt-out — needs a recipient-initiated trigger) or 'marketing' (consent-gated). Filter by pipeline, channel, or a search string. This is the programmatic equivalent of the dashboard's communication picker.

controlState tells you what the Control currently IS, and therefore what editing it will cost: 'winner' (won an experiment, unedited — editing needs an explicit intent), 'winner_edited' (won, then changed since), 'in_experiment' (frozen, an experiment is measuring it right now), 'no_winner' (an experiment ran and settled without one), 'none' (never experimented on). A live letter with no champion is still editable; Publish asks replace vs compete. A champion or a running test: do not edit Control — add a variant, then compete.

pipeline.description: Only return comms in this deliverability pipeline. 'transactional' bypasses marketing opt-out; 'marketing' is consent-gated.

channel.description: Only return comms that include this channel.

search.description: Case-insensitive match against title, subject, and body preview.

tools.name: list_communication_themes
tools.description: List workspace communication Themes (the look: fonts, sizes, colors, Title/Body/Button roles). A Theme is not a Template — Templates are the job (event, slots, copy). Activate a Template with no extra theme step; new emails wear the workspace default theme. Apply writes drafts only; the merchant still publishes each email.

tools.name: create_communication_theme
tools.description: Create a communication Theme (the look). Clone an existing theme with clone_from_id, or pass style/roles. Does not assign other emails. Tell the merchant to publish emails after applying.

tools.name: update_communication_theme
tools.description: Update a communication Theme's name, style tokens, or Title/Body/Button roles. Does not rewrite other emails. Use apply_communication_theme to draft the look onto chosen emails. set_default makes new activations wear this theme.

tools.name: apply_communication_theme
tools.description: Apply a Theme's look onto chosen communication Templates. Default apply is draft — recipients keep the old look until the merchant publishes. apply=live publishes a new version with only the look, so the next send uses it; other unpublished edits stay drafts unless their ids are in publish_edits_ids. Only pass publish_edits_ids when the merchant asked to publish those edits: it sends unreviewed words and blocks to recipients. An email with a second version drafted, unresolved tokens, or a missing app URL keeps its edits as a draft (editsKept in the result). Emails in a running test are skipped (reason in_test) and keep their look. Emails Apex couldn't check for a running test are skipped (reason unchecked) and nothing changes on them: retry those ids, and only if the merchant says they aren't in a test, pass them in confirm_not_in_test_ids. Omit comm_ids to target every template already on this theme. Never group emails by experiment catalog ids; a workspace's order-updates series is the same object.

tools.name: edit_communication
tools.description:
Update a communication's subject, body, CTA, channels, or status. Pass the communication ID and the fields to update. For blank/builder comms, the headline/body/ctaLabel/ctaUrl slots are synced into the rendered email body — verify with preview_communication.

A communication's Control is protected when it won an experiment or a published journey is sending it. Editing it then requires `intent`: "compete" adds your edit as a variant and measures it against the current content (nothing changes for recipients yet); "replace" makes your edit what everyone receives and supersedes any prior win. WHEN IN DOUBT, USE "compete" — it is recoverable, "replace" discards a measured result permanently. The server returns 409 intent_required with both options if you omit it.

slots.description: Content overrides: headline, body, ctaLabel, ctaUrl. These now sync into the rendered email body (not just metadata). Picture: imageUrl (public PNG/JPG/GIF URL; "" removes it), imageAlt, imageHeight (display px), imageNaturalWidth + imageNaturalHeight (the file's real pixel size, so tall art is not stretched to full width). Sets the letter's first image, adding one under the brand header when there is none.

id.description: The section's id from get_communication. Pass it back unchanged so the section keeps its saved settings. Leave it out for a new section. Required for keep.

kind.description: keep only: what the kept section is (e.g. repeater). Read-only; it is ignored on edit.

text.description: heading: the words. text: HTML limited to p, ul, ol, li, strong, em, u, b, i, and <a href="..."> links (https, mailto, a /path in the app, or a {{token}}). No other attributes. {{first_name ?? "friend"}} style tokens work.

url.description: image: public image URL. button: where it goes, e.g. {{app_url}}/experiments.

html.description: html block: sent as written. Use for a plain text link line.

color.description: divider: its own hex color. Leave out to use the theme's.

thickness.description: divider: its own thickness in px (1-8). Leave out to use the theme's.

blocks.description: Rewrite the whole letter body as sections, in order: heading, text, image, button, html, spacer, divider, keep. Keeps the brand header and footer; replaces everything between them. Use this for a multi-section letter (several pictures, subheadings, buttons). To change an existing letter, start from get_communication: pass each section's id back so it keeps its saved settings, and pass every keep section back as it is (a list of people or items, for example), in the place you want it. A keep section left out is removed. Ignores slots when set.

audience_bucket.description: Who this send is for. Default production. Never All or Unclassified.

intent.description: How to apply the edit when the Control is protected. "compete" = add it as a variant and run it as an experiment against the current content (safe default; the current content keeps sending). "replace" = update what everyone receives, superseding any prior win. Required only when the comm won an experiment or is live in a published journey.

confirm_live_experiment.description: Edit a communication that is the treatment in a RUNNING experiment. Marks the numbers untrustworthy: we will not call a winner and we will not learn from mixed counts. Only pass true when they picked an out.

tools.name: reset_communication
tools.description: Put the Apex template's current version into a communication's draft, replacing its copy and layout. Use when a letter was made from an Apex template and the template has since improved, or the stored copy is broken. Works on any communication made from an Apex template, including lists of people or items that edit_communication can't reach. Only the draft changes; nothing sends differently until publish_communication (intent "replace" sends it to everyone and moves its journeys onto it). Refuses while the letter is in a running test. Returns no_template when the letter wasn't made from an Apex template.

tools.name: publish_communication
tools.description:
Publish a communication's draft as the live version — this is what makes an edit reach recipients. Editing only saves a draft.

Compete (or publishing a letter that already has variants) creates a prefilled DRAFT experiment. It does not start the test. After the user reviews the draft, call activate_experiment to begin it. Replace publishes the letter for everyone and never creates an experiment.

Optional overrides: hypothesis, belief_id, confidence, duration_days.

Two conflicts need a decision rather than a retry. `ambiguous_experiment_host` means several published journeys send this communication — the candidates are returned; ask the user and re-issue with host_journey_id. `comm_already_in_experiment` means one is already running; end it first.

`test_check_unavailable` means Apex couldn't check whether the communication is in a running test, so nothing changed. Retry once. If it still fails, ask the user; pass confirmLiveExperiment only when they say it isn't in a test.

intent.description: How to apply the draft when the Control is protected. "compete" = the current content keeps sending and your draft becomes a filled-in experiment draft (then activate_experiment). "replace" = your draft becomes what everyone receives. Required only when the comm won an experiment or is live in a published journey.

confirm_live_experiment.description: Publish over a communication that is the treatment in a RUNNING experiment. Marks the numbers untrustworthy: we will not call a winner and we will not learn from mixed counts. Only pass true when they picked an out.

host_journey_id.description: Which published journey hosts the experiment. Only needed after a 409 ambiguous_experiment_host, using one of the returned candidate ids.

opt_out_journey_ids.description: Journeys that should keep sending the version they send today. Every other journey that sends this communication switches to the new version. Leave out to switch them all.

hypothesis.description: Override the Suggested hypothesis on the draft experiment.

belief_id.description: Link the draft experiment to an existing belief.

duration_days.description: Override the prefilled decision window in days.

tools.name: get_communication
tools.description: Read one communication as written: title, status, channels, subject, and its body as the same sections edit_communication takes in `blocks` (heading, text, image, button, html, spacer, divider). Each section has an id. A section these types can't describe (a list of people or items, a product grid) comes back as keep with its kind. Read, change, and pass the sections back to edit_communication, ids and keep sections included, to edit a letter without losing its pictures, lists or layout. The brand header and footer are not listed; edits keep them. Shows the unpublished draft when there is one.

tools.name: preview_communication
tools.description: See the rendered communication with your brand and Theme applied. Returns the subject, the rendered plain-text body, every picture's URL and size in order, Title/Body/Button roles, which blocks override the theme, and a browser preview link.

tools.name: add_communication_variant
tools.description: Add a content variant (Variant A, B, …) to a communication. Clones the current Control into a new column so you can run a content experiment. When the letter is a champion, this is how you author a challenger — do not edit Control. Does not change what recipients get until you publish. Theme look is inherited; do not set per-block align here.

communication_id.description: The communication to add a variant to

tools.name: send_test_communication
tools.description: Send a test email to yourself. The email will be sent to the logged-in user's email address.

tools.name: trigger_communication
tools.description: Manually send a communication to a specific recipient. Use for one-off sends or testing with specific email addresses.

merge_data.description: Template variables to merge (e.g. user_name, company)

tools.name: create_comm_experiment
tools.description: Legacy helper. Prefer the composer loop: edit_communication or add_communication_variant, then publish_communication (compete creates a prefilled draft), then activate_experiment to start the test. Do not teach this as the default.

funnel_goal.description: The conversion event to optimize for (e.g. 'purchase', 'signup_complete')

tools.name: wire_audience_seed
tools.description: Apex — Wire up the events and traits a campaign audience seed depends on. Use this when the merchant says "wire up the active customers audience" or after the AudienceActivationWizard's Screen 1 hands off to Cursor. Returns the per-event/trait code snippets, the file recommendations, and fires a test event with is_test=1 so the wizard's polling loop confirms the wiring landed end-to-end. Idempotent: calling twice does NOT double-instrument; the agent should still review existing code before adding the snippet.

seed_id.description: Audience seed id, e.g. 'aud-seed-active-customers-90d'. Returned by the seed-campaign-defaults POST endpoint and surfaced in the wizard's URL.

framework.description: Code style to return. Defaults to 'typescript' (the SDK's canonical surface). Use 'snippet' for script-tag installs (Shopify, WordPress, Webflow). The wizard sets this from the detected framework.

fire_test_event.description: When true (default), fires a test event with is_test=1 for each event the seed depends on. The wizard's poll loop sees these and advances. Set to false if the agent only wants to read the snippets without writing test data.

tools.name: wire_audience
tools.description: Apex — Wire up the events and traits ANY audience depends on, not just starter audiences. Use this for bespoke / merchant-built audiences (e.g. 'New sign-ups in the last 14 days', 'Stalled sign-ups — no connector in 12h'). Walks the audience's predicate server-side, classifies each referenced event (auto-fired by the Apex snippet vs documented in Apex's event taxonomy vs custom merchant event), returns per-event recommendations, and optionally fires test events (is_test=1) for non-auto-fired events so the wizard's polling loop confirms wiring landed.

audience_id.description: Segment id (the workspace's saved group). Use list_segments first to find it. Bespoke segments carry generated ids; seed-cloned segments carry ids starting with `aud-seed-`.

framework.description: Code style to return. Defaults to 'typescript'. Use 'snippet' for script-tag installs (Shopify, WordPress, Webflow).

fire_test_event.description: When true (default), fires a test event with is_test=1 for each NON-AUTO-FIRED event the audience depends on. Auto-fired events (pageview, click, etc.) are skipped — they're already firing automatically and don't need a synthetic test.

tools.name: audit_audience_readiness
tools.description: Apex — Check whether an audience is wired up and matching users. Use this to verify your wire_audience_seed work succeeded, or to diagnose why a campaign is showing zero matches. Returns the audience predicate, current matching count, recency buckets, and which referenced events have arrived from the workspace.

audience_id.description: Segment id (the workspace's saved group, not the seed). Use list_segments first to find it.

tools.name: create_journey
tools.description: Apex — Create a blank draft journey (an unconfigured event trigger wired to an exit). Then set_journey_trigger and add_journey_step to build it, and publish_journey to launch. For e-commerce flows like cart recovery, prefer create_journey_from_template. audience_bucket defaults to production (live customers). Same email on TestFlight and the store is two people — do not create a staging copy of the journey.

audience_bucket.description: Who this journey enrolls. Default production. Never All or Unclassified.

tools.name: create_journey_from_template
tools.description: Apex — Instantiate a starter journey template (e.g. Abandoned Cart Recovery) into a fresh draft. Get the templateId from get_wiring_status (Ready-to-run templates list their id). After instantiating, review the steps, then publish_journey.

tools.name: list_trigger_contracts
tools.description: Apex — List the workspace's trigger contracts (the event bindings you pass to set_journey_trigger / add_journey_exit). Returns each contract's id + the event it fires on. Call this before set_journey_trigger so you use a real id instead of guessing.

tools.name: set_journey_trigger
tools.description: Apex — Set the entry trigger (the event that enrolls subjects) on a draft journey's trigger step. Pass event_name (the Apex Spec event, e.g. user_signed_up). A trig-* contract id is storage-only — prefer the Spec name.

event_name.description: Apex Spec event name that enrolls subjects (e.g. user_signed_up). Preferred.

trigger_contract_id.description: Storage id from list_trigger_contracts. Prefer event_name.

tools.name: add_journey_step
tools.description: Apex — Append a Wait or Send to a draft Adaptive Journey. Prefer compose_adoption_milestone for a Milestone (one Wait until they finish, letters already on the arms). Wait mode duration (ISO, e.g. P1D) or until_event (trigger_contract_id + deadline_iso). Send arm event|deadline puts the letter on that Wait arm. Do not add_journey_step send on a compose-built path — use set_journey_send to point the existing Send.

duration_iso.description: wait duration: ISO-8601, e.g. 'P1D' (1 day), 'PT2H' (2 hours).

trigger_contract_id.description: wait until_event: the done-event trigger contract.

deadline_iso.description: wait until_event: hours or days as ISO-8601, e.g. 'PT1H', 'P3D'.

comm_id.description: send only: the communication id to fire (create_communication or an existing comm).

channels.description: send only: channels to fire (default ['email']). Use the SAME tokens as create_communication (email, in_app_push, mobile_push) so a comm's channels map cleanly onto the send step; web_push is send-only.

arm.description: send only: put this Send on the until_event Wait's event or deadline arm.

tools.name: set_journey_send
tools.description: Apex — Point a draft journey's send step at a communication. Use after create_communication + edit_communication so the letter on the journey is yours, not the shared starter template. If the journey has one send, that send is updated. If it has several, pass step_id.

step_id.description: Required when the journey has more than one send.

tools.name: add_journey_branch
tools.description: Apex — Insert a CONDITIONAL content branch before the exit: evaluate one condition and send a different communication to each side. Use this for true content branching (e.g. "cart value > $100 → VIP email, else standard email"). For the simpler "skip the next send if they already converted" case, use add_journey_exit instead. The condition is an attribute test (field_path + operator + value) or an event test (event_fired / event_not_fired within a window).

field_path.description: attribute only: dotted path, e.g. 'cart.valueCents' or 'plan'.

value.description: attribute only: the comparison value (omit for exists/not_exists).

event_name.description: event only: the canonical event, e.g. 'purchase'.

window_days.description: event only: look-back window in days (omit = ever).

when_true_comm_id.description: Communication to send when the condition matches.

when_false_comm_id.description: Communication to send when it doesn't match (omit to just continue to exit).

tools.name: publish_journey
tools.description: Apex — Publish a draft journey so it runs on live trigger events. SAFETY: defaults to a dry-run (validation only) — pass confirmLive:true to actually publish to real customers. Email sends require a verified sender domain or publish is blocked. If this path is already live or a test is measuring it, stop and ask. Do not pass confirmTreatmentChange unless they picked an out.

confirm_live.description: Set true to publish for real. Omitted/false = dry-run validation only.

confirm_treatment_change.description: Publish anyway when this path is live or a test is measuring it. Only pass true after they picked an out.

tools.name: archive_journey
tools.description: Apex — Archive a journey so it stops starting for new people. Same as Archive on the Journeys page: history and records are kept, people already partway through finish, and restore brings it back. A draft that was never published has nothing to keep, so it cannot be archived; pass deleteDraft:true to delete it instead (same as Delete on the Journeys page). If the journey is live or a test is measuring it, stop and ask. Do not pass confirmLiveJourney unless they picked an out.

delete_draft.description: If the journey was never published, delete the draft. Omitted/false = leave the draft alone and say so.

confirm_live_journey.description: Archive anyway when this journey is live or a test is measuring it. Only pass true after they picked an out.

tools.name: archive_communication
tools.description: Apex — Archive a letter (communication template). Same as Archive on the Communications page: it leaves the picker and lists, history and sends are kept, and it can be restored. If a published journey still sends it, Apex refuses and names those journeys, because their Send steps would fail; archive or repoint the journeys first, or pass confirmJourneyRefs:true when they said to archive anyway. If a test is measuring the letter, stop and ask. Do not pass confirmLiveExperiment unless they picked an out.

confirm_journey_refs.description: Archive even though published journeys still send this letter. Only pass true after they said so.

confirm_live_experiment.description: Archive anyway while a test is measuring this letter. Only pass true after they picked an out.

tools.name: create_communication
tools.description: Apex — Create a blank custom communication (draft, no send path) you can reference from a journey send step. Distinct from generate_communications, which generates pre-written messages from catalog templates; use this when you need a net-new message (e.g. a cart-recovery email not in the catalog). audience_bucket defaults to production.

audience_bucket.description: Who this send is for. Default production. Never All or Unclassified.

tools.name: list_journeys
tools.description: Apex — List every adaptive journey in the active workspace. Returns id, name, status (draft/published/paused/archived), and journey type (lifecycle/campaign). Foundation for exit-rule audit loops + journey CRUD agent flows.

tools.name: get_journey
tools.description: Apex — Read the full configuration for a single journey, including steps, goal event, attribution window, and exit rules. Use after list_journeys to inspect a journey's wiring before recommending edits.

tools.name: list_journey_exits
tools.description: Apex — Just the exit-rules block of one journey. Cheaper than get_journey for audit loops that only need to know "does this journey suppress purchase / unsubscribe?".

tools.name: add_journey_exit
tools.description: Apex — Append a new exit rule to a journey's draft. Rule fires when the chosen trigger contract's event lands on a contact with an in-flight execution — Apex stops the execution and skips any pending sends. Re-publish required for the rule to take effect on live runs.

tools.name: remove_journey_exit
tools.description: Apex — Remove an exit rule from a journey's draft. Re-publish required for the change to apply to live runs.

tools.name: get_contact_cart
tools.description: Apex — Read the rolled-up cart state for a contact (Phase 2 of Journey Exit Semantics). Returns lines, itemCount, valueCents, and last-updated timestamp. Useful for "is this lead worth a follow-up?" agent loops.

tools.name: audit_journey_exits
tools.description: Apex — Audit every published journey in the workspace for exit-rule hygiene. Flags marketing/lifecycle journeys (goalEventName=in_app_purchase) that don't have a purchase exit rule — the most common misconfiguration that produces "received the recovery push AFTER converting" complaints.

tools.name: list_segments
tools.description: Apex — List the workspace's segments (saved groups of customers over your own events + traits).

tools.name: get_segment
tools.description: Apex — Fetch one segment by id.

tools.name: create_segment
tools.description: Apex — Create a segment from friendly "conditions" (compiled server-side) OR a raw predicate. Conditions grammar: match all|any of groups; each group match all|any of conditions; each condition is an event ({verb:"has"|"hasnt", event, window_days?}) or a trait ({attribute, op:"is"|"is_not"|"exists", value?}). This is the same grammar the dashboard chip builder speaks.

tools.name: list_adoption_milestones
tools.description: Apex — List the workspace's adoption milestones (per-feature "has this user adopted X?" definitions). A milestone is NOT a goal. Each row now includes enrollMode (all vs future) and gapPolicy.hours when the wait is sub-day.

tools.name: get_adoption_milestone
tools.description: Apex — Fetch one adoption milestone by id.

tools.name: create_adoption_milestone
tools.description: Apex — Create an adoption milestone. "Adopted" is one event or one trait. Omit adopted_when_kind to create the milestone before its finishing moment is chosen, then set it later with update_adoption_milestone; a milestone with no moment counts nobody, mails nobody, and cannot be turned on. Default enroll_mode is "future" (only people who sign up after this is created). Use enroll_mode="all" to include everyone already here. gap_hours wins over gap_days. Starts OFF unless active=true.

action_label.description: Sentence verb: hasn't {action_label}. Never the raw event key.

adopted_when_kind.description: How adoption is detected. Omit to decide the finishing moment later; the milestone stays inert until it is set.

event_name.description: event kind: the event whose firing means adopted

trait_path.description: trait kind: dotted trait path, e.g. 'plan'

order.description: 0-based sequence order (which milestone accounts reach first). Ordering the full set unlocks the account-view Path funnel.

gap_days.description: Nudge this many days after the anchor if not adopted. Ignored when gap_hours is set. Default 3.

gap_hours.description: Nudge this many hours after the anchor. Use for same-day QA. 0 = right away.

gap_kind.description: Anchor. Default days_since_signup. event_not_fired needs since_event_name.

since_event_name.description: event_not_fired: the event the wait starts from.

enroll_mode.description: future (default) = only people who sign up from now on. all = historical roster too.

finish_when.description: this_person (default) = only that person finishes. anyone_here = first person on the same Account finishes it for the company. Event finishes only.

active.description: Turn the milestone on. Default false.

tools.name: update_adoption_milestone
tools.description: Apex — Update an adoption milestone (finishing moment, name, priority, active, gap days/hours, enroll mode, who finishing counts, nudge journey). Pass adopted_when_kind plus event_name or trait_path to set the finishing moment on a milestone created without one. active=true is REFUSED while there is no moment, because nobody could ever finish it and everyone would stay late forever. Changing the moment resets the lift window. If the Milestone is ON, changing what "finished" means stops and asks — do not pass confirmLiveMilestone unless they picked an out. A Milestone keeps BOTH letters on its one Adaptive Journey: the Celebration is a Send on the finish arm, not a second journey. finish_when=anyone_here on a live event Milestone backfills leftover Nudges for Accounts that already have a doer.

adopted_when_kind.description: Set the finishing moment. Changing it resets the lift window.

event_name.description: event kind: the event whose firing means adopted

trait_path.description: trait kind: dotted trait path, e.g. 'plan'

order.description: 0-based sequence order. Prefer reorder_adoption_milestones to sequence the whole set.

finish_when.description: this_person = only that person. anyone_here = first person on the Account. Event finishes only.

nudge_clocks.description: Every clock, in order: first is the wait before the Nudge, later ones are the waits before each extra Nudge. Rewrites the waits on the milestone's Adaptive Journey draft; publish the journey for live letters to use them.

confirm_live_milestone.description: Change an ON Milestone anyway. Only pass true after they picked an out.

tools.name: delete_adoption_milestone
tools.description: Apex — Delete an adoption milestone. If it is on, stop and ask. Do not pass confirmLiveMilestone unless they picked an out.

confirm_live_milestone.description: Delete an ON Milestone anyway. Only pass true after they picked an out.

tools.name: compose_adoption_milestone
tools.description: Apex — Create a Milestone and stamp ONE Adaptive Journey (Trigger → Wait until they finish → Celebration and/or Nudge). scaffold="both" (default) includes both letters; "nudge" / "celebration" one letter; "none" is just-track. Unique Communication per Send — never reuse the shared catalog letters. New milestones default to enroll_mode="future". Journeys are drafts — preview, then publish_journey. A Milestone is NOT a Target.

event_name.description: event kind: the event whose firing means adopted

trait_path.description: trait kind: dotted trait path, e.g. 'plan'

gap_days.description: First Nudge window in days. Ignored when gap_hours or nudge_clocks is set. Default 3.

gap_hours.description: First Nudge window in hours. 0 = right away.

nudge_clocks.description: Each clock is N hours or N days. First is the Wait deadline; later are extra Nudges.

enroll_mode.description: future (default) = only people who sign up from now on.

finish_when.description: this_person (default) = only that person finishes. anyone_here = first person on the same Account. Event finishes only.

active.description: Turn the milestone on. Default false.

scaffold.description: Which letters to include. Default both.

journey_name.description: Name for the Adaptive Journey. Default is the Milestone name.

save_not_yet_segment.description: Save the live not-yet rule as a Segment.

save_done_segment.description: Save the live done rule as a Segment.

tools.name: attach_adoption_milestone_still
tools.description: Apex — Attach a still of the empty screen (not_yet) or the finished screen (done) to a Milestone. Same two pictures the owner uploads. Pass imageBase64 or a public url. For a signed-in product page, capture on their machine with `npx @apex-inc/mcp-server screenshot --milestone … --state not_yet|done --url … --storage-state <login file>` — do not use hosted recapture. A Milestone is NOT a Target.

milestone_id.description: The Milestone to attach the still to

state.description: not_yet = empty screen; done = finished screen

tools.name: recapture_adoption_milestone_stills
tools.description: Apex — Capture the Not yet and Done stills from public pages on a named workspace host. Not localhost. A login wall fails honestly and writes nothing. For a signed-in product page, sit it on their machine: `npx @apex-inc/mcp-server screenshot --milestone … --storage-state <login file>`. Same two pictures the owner uploads.

milestone_id.description: The Milestone to capture stills for

not_yet_url.description: Public https URL of the empty screen.

done_url.description: Public https URL of the finished screen.

tools.name: list_adoption_milestone_stills
tools.description: Apex — List the Not yet and Done stills attached to a Milestone. Empty means they have not attached one yet.

milestone_id.description: The Milestone to list stills for

tools.name: reorder_adoption_milestones
tools.description: Apex — Set the sequence order of adoption milestones in one call. Pass the milestone ids in the desired order; each gets order = its index. Ordering the full set unlocks the "Path" funnel in the account view (a step-by-step drop-off chart that is only honest over an explicitly-ordered set).

ordered_ids.description: Milestone ids in the desired order (index becomes the order).

tools.name: get_adoption_metrics
tools.description: Apex — Aggregated adoption metrics: per-milestone funnel + lift-vs-holdout, plus workspace health. Counts only (no user PII).

tools.name: get_adoption_account_progress
tools.description: Apex — One Account's Path: which Milestones this company has finished, who did them, and how many people are Not yet / Started / Done. account_id is the company id from identify({ account: { id } }). Never includes holdout.

account_id.description: The Account id (identify account.id or the Apex acct_ id)

tools.name: get_adoption_user_progress
tools.description: Apex — One person's Path (Not yet / Started / Done) across every active Milestone. Includes finish_when and inherited when Anyone here finished for their company. Never email, name, or holdout. end_user_id must be a valid user id, not an email.

end_user_id.description: The end-user id to look up (not an email address)

tools.name: list_adoption_features
tools.description: Apex — List the workspace's tenant-owned feature groupings (how adoption milestones group your own events).

tools.name: create_adoption_feature
tools.description: Apex — Create or upsert (by key) a tenant-owned feature grouping. Group your own events under a named feature the milestone builder can target.

key.description: Stable key; slugged from label if omitted

event_names.description: Event names tagged into this feature

tools.name: list_partner_programs
tools.description: List every affiliate program this merchant owns. Returns each program's name, status (active/paused/archived), visibility (public/private), approval mode, commission structure, reputation counters, and created/updated timestamps.

tools.name: create_partner_program
tools.description: Create a new affiliate program. Partners can join via marketplace (public+auto), by invite only (private), or via application (public+manual). Commission can be a flat CPA amount or a percentage of sale (RevShare).

name.description: Public program name, shown in marketplace + partner portal

appliesTo.description: Which conversion event pays the commission

tools.name: update_partner_program
tools.description: Update an existing program (pause/resume, change visibility, edit default commission). Changing default commission does NOT apply to existing members — use apply_program_default_to_members for that.

updates.description: Fields to update: name, description, status, visibility, commissionStructure, vertical, tagline, landingPageUrl, autoPayoutPolicy, etc.

tools.name: list_partner_program_members
tools.description: List every partner bound to a specific program. Shows each member's handle, current commission (with source: program_default | membership_override | invite_override), totalEarnedUsd, approvedConversions count.

tools.name: apply_program_default_to_members
tools.description: Apply the program's current default commission to every existing member whose commission is a program_default source. Members with sticky overrides (membership_override / invite_override) are NOT touched. Fires partner_commission_changed emails to affected partners.

tools.name: update_membership_rate
tools.description: Override a single partner's commission rate on this merchant's program. Sticky — survives future program default updates. Opens the per-membership commission history with `source: membership_override` for audit.

reason.description: Audit log note — e.g. 'Volume discount Q3 2026'

tools.name: reset_membership_rate
tools.description: Reset a partner's commission back to the program default, removing any prior override. Useful when a negotiated rate expires or a promo ends.

tools.name: invite_partner
tools.description: Send a magic-link invite to a partner for a specific program. Resolves existing profiles by email (no duplicate profile created) or creates a pending invite the partner redeems on first sign-in. Optional customRate overrides the program default for this partner's membership.

email.description: Partner's email — used for matching + the invite email

inviter_name.description: Name shown in the invite email's 'from' field

inviter_message.description: Personal note from the merchant, shown in the invite email

custom_rate.description: Override commission for this partner only (sticky)

tools.name: list_pending_payouts
tools.description: Every approved-but-unpaid commission this merchant owes, grouped into aging buckets: 0-30 / 30-60 / 60+ days. Returns totals per bucket + the effective autoPayoutPolicy + current merchant cap. Use before approving batches to see the backlog.

tools.name: approve_payouts
tools.description: Approve one or more pending payouts. Each approved conversion: transitions to 'approved', writes a HoldbackEntry splitting commission into available + held portions per tier policy (25% held for NEW, 15% TRUSTED, 5% VERIFIED), stamps approvedAt. Transfer fires later via the scheduled payout orchestrator (run-payouts cron).

tools.name: reject_payouts
tools.description: Reject pending payouts (e.g. suspicious patterns that don't warrant a FraudCase). Flips conversions to 'reversed'. Also opens a low-severity audit FraudCase per rejection so patterns surface if the same partner's payouts get rejected repeatedly.

reason.description: Shown in the audit case — e.g. 'Duplicate event'

tools.name: get_effective_fees
tools.description: Show the merchant's current fee schedule for every fee kind (facilitation_payout, identity_verification, instant_payout). Returns bps + flatUsd + source (platform_default | merchant_override | hardcoded_fallback) + isCustom flag. Useful for building pricing disclosure UIs or answering 'what am I charged?'.

tools.name: vouch_for_partner
tools.description: Vouch for a partner — bumps their trust tier by one level (NEW→TRUSTED or TRUSTED→VERIFIED) for 60 days. REQUIRES indemnityAcknowledged=true: if the partner commits fraud during the vouched window, your merchant account is liable for any clawback the reserve can't cover. Fails if the partner is already VERIFIED.

indemnity_acknowledged.description: Must be exactly `true` — acknowledges merchant liability for fraud during vouch window

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: Apex — List the workspace's ACTIVE events: the canonical event names actually firing, with total volume and the platforms they arrive on, from the ingest catalog. Use this to discover which events exist / are wired before choosing a primary metric or guardrail in create_experiment, or to confirm an event is live. Distinct from list_metrics (which lists typed rate/revenue/duration GOALS) — this is the raw observed-event catalog.

limit.description: Max events to return, by volume descending (default 50).

tools.name: list_metrics
tools.description: Apex — List the canonical metric/goal catalog for this workspace: typed metrics (rate/revenue/duration) with whether each is DETECTED (firing, with volume) and its outcome tier. Use this to pick a measurable OUTCOME goal (purchase/signup) over a proxy (email_open) before create_experiment, or role:'guardrail' to see protective harm signals.

only_measurable.description: Only return metrics the engine can estimate today (default true).

role.description: Filter to goal metrics (optimize) or guardrail metrics (protect against harm).

tools.name: get_growth_reality
tools.description: Apex — "Is our growth real?" Per goal, the cumulative lift of everything Apex did (journeys + experiments) vs a persistent do-nothing global holdout, with a 95% CI. The honest, holdout-gated answer to "would this have happened anyway?" Forward-only; goals still collecting are flagged, not faked.

days.description: Trailing window in days, or 'all' for since-inception (default).

tools.name: get_channel_economics
tools.description: Apex — "Where should my next dollar go?" Per acquisition channel (raw first-touch): LTGP:CAC (lifetime gross profit over CAC) where the merchant reports product cost, LTV:CAC (lifetime revenue over CAC) everywhere else, plus payback months, CAC, and customers, split into Acquisition (paid) vs Leverage (owned/organic, no spend). Computed from real contacts + spend + revenue — metrics with missing inputs are shown as "—", never fabricated. Free intelligence; the verdict is never gated.

days.description: Trailing window in days, or 'all' for since-inception (default).

tools.name: get_saas_recurring_revenue
tools.description: Apex — SaaS recurring-revenue economics: MRR, ARR, the monthly waterfall (new / expansion / reactivation / contraction / churn — accounting-identity tested), and NRR/GRR for the last complete month. Computed from materialized monthly snapshots (calendar months, UTC); the current month is flagged in-progress. NRR/GRR read "collecting history" until 13 months of snapshots exist — never fabricated.

months.description: Months of waterfall history to include (2-36, default 13).

start.description: Explicit window start, YYYY-MM-DD (mapped to calendar months; use with end — overrides months).

end.description: Explicit window end, YYYY-MM-DD (use with start).

tools.name: get_saas_expansion
tools.description: Apex — SaaS expansion economics: expansion vs contraction MRR for the last complete month, accounts expanding (counts — small-n honest), and seat growth from seat_count. Metrics with missing inputs come back null, never fabricated.

months.description: Months of series history to include (2-36, default 13).

start.description: Explicit window start, YYYY-MM-DD (mapped to calendar months; use with end — overrides months).

end.description: Explicit window end, YYYY-MM-DD (use with start).

tools.name: get_ecommerce_product_sales
tools.description: Apex — E-commerce product sales: top products by revenue with the per-product view → add-to-cart → purchase funnel and refund counts. Products need a product_id on commerce events; never-wired signals are reported as unwired, not zero.

days.description: Trailing window in days (default 90, max 396 — the 13-month event log).

start.description: Explicit window start, YYYY-MM-DD (use with end — overrides days).

end.description: Explicit window end, YYYY-MM-DD (use with start).

tools.name: list_product_costs
tools.description: Apex — What each product costs, and which ones Apex has no cost for. Lists every SKU with a declared cost PLUS every SKU the merchant's orders have sold in the last 30 days, so an uncosted product is visible rather than merely absent. Apex reports gross profit and LTGP:CAC only where cost is known, so the uncosted rows are the gap worth closing. Two columns matter: "orders" is the per-unit cost the merchant's own purchase events reported (preferred — it tracks their real costs over time), "declared" is a standing cost set in Apex that fills orders reporting none. Use this before set_product_cost so you never overwrite a cost that is already right.

uncosted_only.description: Only SKUs with no cost from either route — the actionable list.

tools.name: set_product_cost
tools.description: Apex — Declare what one product costs per unit, so Apex can report gross profit on orders that didn't carry a cost of their own. PREFER instrumenting unit_cost on purchase line items instead where you can: an order carries the cost that was true when it happened, whereas a standing cost declared here is a snapshot that goes stale silently. Use this to backfill history, or for a SKU whose checkout can't report cost. NEVER invent or estimate a cost — a fabricated margin looks measured and is not, and the merchant has no way to tell downstream. Ask them for the number. Rules: the cost is PER UNIT (not a line total), it never overrides a cost an order reported for itself, and it never applies backward before effective_from.

item_key.description: The product identifier Apex knows this SKU by — the product_id or sku on the merchant's order lines. Get it from list_product_costs.

cost_usd.description: Cost PER UNIT in USD. A four-figure value on a low-priced item is usually cents typed as dollars; values above 1000000 are refused.

effective_from.description: ISO date the cost applies from. Defaults to NOW, which is deliberate — defaulting backward would restate the merchant's whole order history at today's supplier price. Pass an explicit date only when they know the older price.

name.description: Display name, if Apex has no name for this SKU yet.

tools.name: upload_product_catalog
tools.description: Apex — Tell Apex what the merchant sells, in bulk, BEFORE the first sale. Every other way a product reaches Apex needs a sale to have happened already, so a merchant setting up pre-launch has a catalog Apex knows nothing about. Use this when you can read their catalog from somewhere — a products table, a Shopify/Stripe export, a CSV they hand you. NEVER invent, estimate, or derive a cost from a price: a fabricated margin looks measured and nobody downstream can tell. Ask them, or send only the fields you actually know. cost_usd is applied to orders that report no cost of their own, from effective_from forward. price_usd is reference only — revenue, LTV and gross profit always come from what orders actually report, so a price here can never distort them; it makes the catalog complete before launch and lets Apex flag it when real orders disagree with it. Re-running with the same data is safe. Max 500 products per call — page through a larger catalog. This does not replace instrumenting unit_cost on purchase line items, which stays the durable fix because an order then carries the cost that was true when it happened; a catalog cost is a snapshot that goes stale silently.

item_key.description: The identifier the merchant's ORDERS will send for this SKU — their product_id or sku. If this doesn't match what the order lines carry, Apex can't connect the two.

cost_usd.description: What the product costs the MERCHANT, per unit. Omit rather than guess.

price_usd.description: What the merchant SELLS it for, per unit. Reference data — never used as revenue.

effective_from.description: ISO date cost_usd applies from. Defaults to now, which is deliberate — defaulting backward would restate order history at today's supplier price.

products.description: Up to 500 products. Each needs item_key plus at least one of name, cost_usd, price_usd.

tools.name: get_ecommerce_returns
tools.description: Apex — E-commerce returns & refunds: refund rate (money back, order basis), return rate (goods back — separate metric, never summed), reason breakdown, refund cycle time, AOV, and repeat purchase. Refund data lands automatically from Stripe; return_requested / return_completed events power the goods-back story.

days.description: Trailing window in days (default 90, max 396 — the 13-month event log).

start.description: Explicit window start, YYYY-MM-DD (use with end — overrides days).

end.description: Explicit window end, YYYY-MM-DD (use with start).

tools.name: get_marketplace_metrics
tools.description: Apex — Marketplace health across six pillars: liquidity (search→transaction, match rate, zero-result searches, unfulfilled demand), supply & demand balance, economics (GMV vs the take — fee_amount is the platform's revenue, GMV never inflates LTV), buyer retention, trust rates, and concentration risk. Sliceable by category / geo / price_band (low-volume slices are suppressed for privacy). Metrics whose events aren't wired come back as unwired hints, never fabricated zeros.

days.description: Trailing window in days (default 90, max 396 — the 13-month event log).

start.description: Explicit window start, YYYY-MM-DD (use with end — overrides days).

end.description: Explicit window end, YYYY-MM-DD (use with start).

tools.name: track_event
tools.description:
Apex — Track an event through the Apex Spec.

Identical to the SDK's track() and the snippet's apex.track(). Use this to instrument events from agent workflows, CI pipelines, or IDE actions.

The public Spec is one registry (`APEX_EVENTS`): `page_view`, `product_view`, `add_to_cart`, `checkout_started`, `order_placed`, `in_app_purchase`, `user_signed_up`, `waitlist_joined`, `user_invited`, `user_invite_accepted`, `user_identified`, `app_open`, `session_start`, `form_submit`, `feature_used`, `ui_action`. Field names are flat snake_case. Named in-product controls are `ui_action` with `action` + `name` + optional `location`. SDK helper: `trackUiAction({ action, name, location })`.

Custom event names are accepted, but prefer canonical names from GET /api/spec/events so templates, journeys, and conversions wire without aliases. Full spec: https://docs.apex.inc/spec.

Events fired through this tool carry a stable synthetic visitorId (mcp-agent-*, fixed for this MCP process) and a timestamp, so they WILL count toward wiring detection. They are flagged as agent-fired (source: "mcp") — not test-mode. Fire them deliberately.

event.description: Event name — snake_case from the Apex Spec (e.g. 'page_view', 'user_signed_up', 'order_placed'). Custom names are accepted but prefer canonical ones.

properties.description: Flat snake_case properties matching the spec entry for this event (e.g. { product_id: 'prod_abc', value: 29.99, currency: 'USD' }).

tools.name: send_server_event
tools.description: Apex — Server Events API. Send a server-to-server event via the /api/v1/events endpoint (clientType: "server", batch cap 100, idempotency-key supported). Use this from agent workflows that simulate backend integrations (Stripe webhook flows, CRM-driven conversions, billing events) or to test the Server Events API end-to-end. Differs from track_event in that it stamps clientType: "server" and uses the v1 ingest contract.

type.description: Event type (e.g. 'order_placed', 'user_signed_up', or any custom verb)

visitor_id.description: Visitor ID to stitch back to a web/mobile session (apex_vid)

email.description: Email to stitch by identity when no visitorId is known

environment.description: Dashboard slice only. Omit to leave Unclassified. Never use this to force Production dollars.

release_channel.description: Optional OS channel (testflight, app-store, xcode-debug, …). Dashboard slice only.

idempotency_key.description: Stable key to prevent double-counting on retry (defaults to a fresh UUID)

tools.name: identify_user
tools.description: Apex — Identify a user by email for identity stitching. Works identically to the SDK's identify() and the snippet's apex.identify(). Links an anonymous visitor to a known email. Pass avatarUrl (a canonical attribute) to give the Contact a profile photo that renders across Apex — the people list, detail page, and Live widget. The workspace's own word for a person (Customer / Lead / Client / User, from its vertical) is what its dashboard shows; use that word when reporting back.

avatar_url.description: Profile photo URL (https). Maps to the canonical avatar_url attribute; renders across Apex. Validated on write — non-https/invalid URLs are dropped and the UI falls back to initials. From OIDC logins this is the `picture` claim (`photoURL` in Firebase).

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: Apex — Read the workspace's canonical Schema (data dictionary): entities, their fields, which fields are wired (observed in live data) vs not, surface coverage, and any canonical mappings. Use to see what variables/attributes a workspace has and what's still unwired before authoring comms or segments.

tools.name: map_attribute
tools.description: Apex — Map a discovered field onto its canonical Apex Spec name (e.g. firstName -> first_name) so templates resolve it cleanly at send time. Pass canonicalName: null to clear an existing mapping.

entity_key.description: Entity key (user, account, order, product, or a custom entity)

field_name.description: The field to map, as stored (e.g. 'firstName')

canonical_name.description: Canonical snake_case name (e.g. 'first_name'), or null to clear

tools.name: define_event
tools.description: Apex — Define a governed custom event in the workspace's Schema (the customer-extensible registry). Promotes one of the merchant's own events to a first-class, typed, versioned definition that behaves like a canonical Apex Spec event (selectable as a journey trigger/goal, resolvable as comm tokens, validated at ingest). Names must be snake_case and CANNOT shadow a canonical Apex Spec event — call get_event_spec first and reuse the canonical event when one fits. Propose the schema from the merchant's observed payloads (get_schema) and codebase, then confirm with them before defining.

name.description: snake_case event name, not already in the Apex Spec

description.description: One sentence: when this event fires

fields.description: Field name -> type. Types: "string" | "number" | "boolean" | "object" | "array"; append "?" for optional (e.g. {"widget_id":"string","width":"number?"})

scope.description: workspace (default) or org (shared across the org's workspaces)

primary_metric.description: True if this is a conversion/outcome that can be a journey goal

recommended_transport.description: Where to fire it: server for money-truth, client for intent/engagement

tools.name: log_prediction
tools.description: Apex — Log a prediction about a metric change. Feeds the calibration loop. Before calling, present the metric, expected change, and confidence as options the user can pick from or adjust.

expected_change.description: Expected change as a decimal (e.g. 0.15 for +15%)

confidence.description: How sure you are about this prediction (0-100%)

time_horizon.description: Days until the prediction should be evaluated (default: 14)

tools.name: list_data_sources
tools.description: Apex — List the workspace's Data Sources (the producers that send events: Website, iOS/Android apps, Backend). Shows each source's live status (live / listening / stalled / not-started). Call when the user asks "where is my data coming from?", "which sources are live?", or to audit collection coverage.
