include_archived.description: Include archived sources. Defaults to false.

tools.name: create_data_source
tools.description: Apex — Register a new Data Source in the active workspace. Most sources auto-register on their first event; use this to set one up BEFORE events arrive (e.g. a Backend API source). Reporting-only — registering a source never changes access control.

name.description: Display name, e.g. 'Marketing site' or 'Backend API'.

tools.name: get_data_source_health
tools.description: Apex — Get the live status of one Data Source (live / listening / stalled / not-started) plus its first/last seen timestamps. Use to diagnose "why isn't my backend / app showing data?"

tools.name: get_analytics_sources
tools.description: Apex — Unified analytics breakdown by Data Source, platform, and hostname over a date range. Use for "how much traffic from each source?", "web vs mobile split", or "which hostnames are busiest?".

tools.name: get_analytics_hostnames
tools.description: Apex — The hostname catalog for this workspace (every host the web snippet has reported, ranked by volume). Use to populate a hostname filter or audit which subdomains are sending events.

tools.name: get_event_spec
tools.description: Apex — The canonical event reference for instrumenting Apex tracking: every event name, its fields (with required/optional markers), and example payloads, as a JSON Schema bundle. Call this BEFORE wiring apex.track()/Apex.track() calls or Server Events API posts into a codebase so you use canonical names and field shapes. Pair with get_wiring_status to verify your instrumentation afterwards.

event.description: Return only this event's schema (canonical name, e.g. 'add_to_cart'). Omit for the full bundle.

tools.name: get_wiring_status
tools.description: Apex — Live wiring verification for the active workspace: which canonical events have been received (tier: waiting → detected → verified), which identify traits (first_name, email, …) are arriving, per-data-source status, and which journey/communication templates are Ready to run. Call this AFTER instrumenting tracking code to verify your own work — iterate until each wired event reports "detected". Presence-only: never returns end-user values.

tools.name: propose_wiring_plan
tools.description: Apex — Report the Apex Spec instrumentation opportunities you found by SCANNING the merchant's codebase (auth flows → identify + user_signed_up, checkout → purchase events, forms → form_submit, app purchases → in_app_purchase, server order paths → order_placed, …). Call this BEFORE wiring: the plan appears on the merchant's setup page as pending lights, each flipping green when its first real event arrives. Structure your scan report in three sections: (1) ALREADY WIRED — events the repo already instruments (include them here with wired: true; they're awaiting their first heartbeat), (2) GAPS TO WIRE — the work you propose, (3) WON'T WIRE + WHY — opportunities you're deliberately skipping (e.g. a server event with no backend, or a form that already fires a richer dedicated event). Then instrument each gap where the truth lives and verify with get_wiring_status. Scan first; never ask the merchant to enumerate events for you.

name.description: Canonical snake_case event name from the Apex Spec (use get_event_spec), or a custom snake_case name.

surface.description: Where this event should fire FROM — wire each event where the truth lives.

note.description: Short pointer to where you found the opportunity, e.g. 'checkout/confirm.ts handlePayment()'.

wired.description: True when the repo ALREADY instruments this event (awaiting its first heartbeat) — the merchant's board labels it 'wired' instead of 'agent plan'.

events.description: Every instrumentation opportunity found in the scan — both already-wired events (wired: true) and the gaps you propose to wire.

summary.description: One-paragraph scan summary for the merchant — include what you're deliberately NOT wiring and why.

tools.name: apex_test_event
tools.description: Apex — Send a test event through the public ingestion endpoint and confirm it was accepted. The fastest way to verify event tracking works after installing the SDK.

tools.name: apex_recent_events
tools.description: Apex — List recent events for the workspace (optionally filtered by type). Use to debug SDK wiring without opening the dashboard.

tools.name: apex_health
tools.description: Apex — One-shot health check of every connected integration (last sync, status). Use before adding a feature that depends on a connector.

tools.name: apex_spec_validate
tools.description: Apex — Fetch the canonical Apex Spec event taxonomy so you can validate the track()/identify()/useApexVariant() calls in the user's files against it (ESLint-like for Apex usage). Read the user's files, find the calls, and flag event names + attributes that don't match the returned spec.

tools.name: list_conversions
tools.description: Apex — List the workspace's Conversions (owned-event definitions of valued actions, e.g. "Purchase", "Signup"). Call this when the user asks what conversions are defined. The starred primary is a label for that Conversion — it does not pick the funnel stages and it is not the experiment default. Experiments name their own metric; the funnel follows the workspace conversion model.

tools.name: create_conversion
tools.description: Apex — Define a new Conversion (an owned-event definition of a valued action). Most conversions are a custom_event with an eventName (e.g. "order_placed", "user_signed_up") matching an Apex Spec event you send via track. isPrimary stars this Conversion as a label — it does not pick experiment defaults or drive the funnel.

type.description: How the conversion is detected. custom_event is the most common (set eventName).

event_name.description: For custom_event: the Apex Spec event name to match, e.g. 'purchase'.

selector.description: For click/form_submit: a CSS selector to match.

target_url.description: For pageview: the URL (or path) that counts as a completion.

is_primary.description: Make this the primary conversion (only one can be primary).

tools.name: set_primary_conversion
tools.description: Apex — Mark a Conversion as the starred primary. That star labels the Conversion — it does not set experiment defaults or drive the funnel. Experiments name their own metric. Pass the conversion id from list_conversions.

conversion_id.description: The conversion id to promote (from list_conversions).

tools.name: create_target
tools.description: Apex — Create a Target: an aggregate KPI number to hit by a date (MRR, pipeline, "1,000 signups by Q3"). Optionally bind it to a Conversion (sourceConversionId from list_conversions) to auto-count progress from that conversion's completions; otherwise it's a manual number you update yourself.

source_conversion_id.description: Optional: bind to a Conversion (from list_conversions) to auto-track progress.

tools.name: list_audiences
tools.description: Apex — List the buyer lists Apex keeps on the workspace's ad platforms: which segment each is built from, which platforms it goes to, which platforms it actually reached, and how many people it holds back. Same as Attribution → Ad platforms → Who sees your ads.

tools.name: update_audience
tools.description: Apex — Change where a buyer list goes, or how many of its people Apex holds back from the ads. holdout_percent 0 stops holding anyone back. Dropping a platform the list already reached deletes the list on that platform, which cannot be undone, and any ad set using it loses it: ask the owner first and pass confirm_delete only after they said yes. Without it, Apex changes nothing and says which platforms would lose the list. Held-back lists that belong to an Ad holdout can't be changed here.

platforms.description: Every platform the list should go to: meta-ads, google-ads, linkedin-ads (or meta / google / linkedin).

holdout_percent.description: Share of the list's people kept out of the ads: 0, 5, 10 or 20, the same choices as the list card. 0 stops holding anyone back.

confirm_delete.description: Only after the owner said yes to deleting the list on every platform it already reached that platforms leaves out.

tools.name: remove_audience
tools.description: Apex — Take a buyer list off every ad platform it reached and stop sending it. Deleting it on a platform cannot be undone, and an ad set that used it stops using it. Ask the owner first; pass confirm only after they said yes. Reports any platform that refused, so the workspace can delete it there by hand.

confirm.description: Only after the owner said yes to removing this list from every platform.

tools.name: list_audience_removals
tools.description: Apex — People who asked to be deleted or opted out of ads but are still on one of the workspace's buyer lists, because the platform refused or couldn't be reached when Apex took them off. One row per list and platform: `owed` (still on it), `stopped_retrying` (Apex retries every day for 30 days, then stops and waits for the workspace), `why` (not_connected, platform_cant_remove_yet, or platform_refused) and `platform_said`. Empty means nobody is owed. Pass audience_id for one list, or nothing for every list. Same as the amber line on the list card.

audience_id.description: From list_audiences. Leave out for every list.

tools.name: retry_audience_removals
tools.description: Apex — Try again now to take the people who asked to be deleted or opted out off one buyer list, including the ones Apex stopped retrying after 30 days. Use it after the owner reconnects a platform or fixes what the platform refused (see list_audience_removals). Returns how many Apex tried, how many came off, and what is still owed. Admin-only.

tools.name: list_audience_goals
tools.description: Apex — The four things a buyer list can be for, and whether this workspace can make each one now. win_back shows ads to people who bought but not within the workspace's kind-of-business window (`window_days`); stop_paying leaves everyone who ever bought out of ads meant for new people; interested shows ads to people who added to cart or started checkout in the last 30 days and never bought (`locked` until those events arrive); lookalike gives Meta everyone who bought with what each spent, for a value-based lookalike (Meta only). Each goal returns `networks` (where its list can go right now) and `lists` (lists the workspace already made for it). When a goal already has a list, ask whether the workspace wants another before adding one.

tools.name: add_audience
tools.description: Apex — Make a buyer list from a goal (see list_audience_goals) and send it. Apex saves the goal's rule as a segment named after the list, which the owner can change in Segments, makes the list on it, and sends it to each platform; it updates every day after. Nobody is held back. Call list_audience_goals first, tell the owner who goes on the list and where it goes, and pass confirm: true only after they say yes. Refused when the goal is locked, or when none of the platforms can take the list. Admin-only.

platforms.description: Where it goes. Defaults to every platform the goal's list can go to now.

name.description: The list's name. Defaults to the goal's list name.

send_now.description: Send it right away. Defaults to true; false waits for the daily update.

confirm.description: The owner heard who goes and where, and said yes.

tools.name: preview_ad_platform_send
tools.description: Apex — Before sending one of the workspace's events to its ad platforms, see what each platform would hear. Pass the event as the workspace sends it and what it means. Returns each platform's state: sends (hears `word` right away), apex_makes (hears it once Apex makes the conversion there), no_word (the platform has nothing for this meaning, so it is not sent), not_connected, not_agreed (the workspace hasn't agreed to send sales there yet), other_source (the workspace set another tool to send that platform's conversions), held (the owner asked Apex not to send people to any ad platform), coming_soon, or turned_off. `without_consent_answer` says whether an event that carries no consent answer goes out (sent) or not (not_sent); when it's not_sent, tell the owner only events with a yes go. Also returns `estimate`: how often the event happened in the last 30 days, the sends a month that bills (one per event, however many platforms hear it), the workspace's free sends and use this month, and the monthly cost at its price (null when Apex couldn't count; only people Apex knows are sent, so the real number can be lower). Saves and sends nothing. Show the owner the result before anything starts sending.

event_name.description: The event exactly as the workspace sends it, e.g. trial_started.

meaning.description: What the event means: purchase, lead, signup, subscription, add_to_cart, or something_else when none fit.

tools.name: list_ad_platform_sends
tools.description: Apex — The workspace's own events Apex sends to its ad platforms, with what each one means and what each platform hears (same states as preview_ad_platform_send). Sales, signups and leads Apex already knows about go out on their own and are not listed here.

tools.name: add_ad_platform_send
tools.description: Apex — Start sending one of the workspace's events to its ad platforms. Call preview_ad_platform_send first and show the owner what each platform would hear, the 30-day count and the monthly cost; pass confirm: true only after the owner says yes. Saved on the workspace's Conversion for that event (created when there isn't one). Only platforms the workspace has connected and agreed to send to hear it; this tool never agrees for the workspace. For something_else, Apex makes the conversion on Meta so campaigns can optimize for it; the result's `made` lists where it did and `couldnt_make` says why a platform refused (the send still goes). Refused when the event already means something else on Conversions, when Apex already sends it as a sale, or when no platform can hear it yet. Admin-only.

event_name.description: The event exactly as the workspace sends it, e.g. trial_started.

meaning.description: What the event means: purchase, lead, signup, subscription, add_to_cart, or something_else when none fit.

send_value.description: Send the event's amount when it has one. Defaults to true.

name.description: Name for a new Conversion. Defaults to the event name in words.

confirm.description: The owner saw the preview and said yes.

tools.name: remove_ad_platform_send
tools.description: Apex — Stop sending one of the workspace's events to its ad platforms. The Conversion stays, so experiments and goals that count it are untouched, and what the platforms already heard stays with them. Pass the id from list_ad_platform_sends. Admin-only.

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: Apex — List B2B accounts (companies / clients) in the active workspace with rollup LTV, member count, and pipeline. Accounts aggregate every member's revenue into one company-level number. Default sort is by LTV.

search.description: Filter by account name or domain.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Apex — Read one B2B account: rollup counters (account LTV, gross, refunds, purchases), member count, plan, seats, and traits. Account LTV is the sum of every member's directly-billed revenue with no double counting.

tools.name: get_account_people
tools.description: Apex — The member roster for an account: every Contact linked to it (primary members plus sub-account members), with each member's directly-billed revenue, score, and last-active. Per-person dollars are what that member was billed — account LTV is never split across seats.

account_id.description: Internal acct_ id (or a sub-account id).

tools.name: list_sub_accounts
tools.description: Apex — List the sub-accounts (workspaces / teams / projects) that belong to a B2B account (B2B-001). Sub-accounts are the intermediate org-unit layer between an account and its people; each carries a kind label and its own member count.

tools.name: get_contact_groups
tools.description: Apex — The account groups (workspaces / teams) a contact belongs to (B2B-001) — the answer to "which workspaces is this user in?". Returns each group with its kind and the contact's role in it.

tools.name: update_account_pipeline
tools.description: Apex — Log an account-level pipeline (open-deal) value with a note (Sales-Led / Hybrid workspaces). The account number is canonical for reporting when both an account and a contact pipeline value exist.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: List all workspaces available to your API key. Use this to see which workspaces you can work with.

tools.name: switch_workspace
tools.description: Switch the active workspace for this session. All subsequent API calls will use this workspace. After switching, Apex verifies it can read the workspace and warns if authentication or the workspace key looks wrong.

workspace_key.description: The workspace key to switch to.

project_key.description: Deprecated alias of workspaceKey. Use workspaceKey.

tools.name: list_orgs
tools.description: List all organizations you have access to, with their workspaces. Use this to see which orgs and workspaces are available.

tools.name: switch_org
tools.description: Switch the active organization. This also switches to the first workspace in that org.

org_id.description: The organization ID to switch to (from list_orgs)

tools.name: get_setup_state
tools.description: Apex — READ-ONLY. The Set up Apex checklist for the active workspace, the same one the dashboard shows: the next step, every step's status, what each is waiting on, and how to finish it from here (the tool to call, or why a person has to do it in a browser, with the link). Use to answer "where am I in setup?" and "what's next?". Work the next step, then call this again. If first-run is incomplete, name the merchant with update_organization / update_workspace before inventing events. This tool never writes. No tool marks a step complete: steps finish when the real thing happens. When the owner says a step or area is not for them, record it with skip_setup_step or decline_setup_area after they say so.

tools.name: list_workspace_environments
tools.description: Apex — Read the sites this workspace named as Production and Beta, plus unclassified sites Apex has seen. Name sites before you trust the Production slice. Do not invent a second workspace.

tools.name: set_workspace_environments
tools.description: Apex — Name Production sites (and optional Beta sites). Apex will not guess staging. / qa. / dev. Naming reclassifies events from those sites at read time.

beta_hosts.description: Hostnames that are testers. Never guessed from staging.

tools.name: check_workspace_readiness
tools.description: Apex — Check whether the workspace is ready for the Graduation Pipeline flow: Apex auth, GitHub App install, and (if you pass a repo) whether Apex may write to it. Run this at the top of /apex-experiment, /apex-graduate, etc., and resolve any gaps before proceeding.

repo.description: Current repo "owner/name" to check write opt-in for

tools.name: start_apex_login
tools.description: Apex — Mint a stored API key through a browser sign-in, for a server or CI that cannot do browser approval. Not for setting up or connecting this editor: that is browser approval (get_setup_state shows the link, then wait_for_apex_approval). Returns a browser URL and polls until the key is minted. Save it only with the developer's consent, never in a committed file.

tools.name: wait_for_apex_approval
tools.description: Apex — Call this right after showing the user an Apex approval link (the "Apex isn't connected to this editor yet" message). Waits up to 2 minutes and returns the moment they click Approve in the browser, so you can carry on without asking them to tell you. Then retry the call you were making. If nothing is pending it starts a new request and returns the link.

tools.name: start_integration_install
tools.description: Apex — Begin a browser hop to connect GitHub, Stripe, Meta, Google, LinkedIn, TikTok, or Google Analytics. Returns a URL; open it. Legal acknowledgements stay on the opened page — this tool does not confirm them. Polls until connected, same as GitHub.

type.description: github, stripe, meta, google, linkedin, tiktok, or google-analytics. Ads also accept hub names (meta-ads, google-ads, linkedin-ads, tiktok-ads). google means Google Ads.

org_id.description: Required for Stripe Connect. Defaults to the active org.

tools.name: create_server_key
tools.description: Apex — Create an organization server key (apex_sk_) so a backend can send events (send_server_event, POST /api/v1/events). Owners and admins only. The key is shown once: put it straight into the server's secret store or hosting environment secrets. Never commit it, and never use it as this editor's APEX_API_KEY. A personal key from create_api_key cannot send server events.

org_id.description: Organization (from list_orgs). Defaults to the active org.

tools.name: create_api_key
tools.description: Apex — Create a personal Apex API key (apex_uk_) for signing an editor or script in as you. Returns the raw key once. It cannot send server events; use create_server_key for a backend.

tools.name: list_api_keys
tools.description: Apex — List the current user's Apex API keys (names + ids; never the secret).

tools.name: revoke_api_key
tools.description: Apex — Revoke (delete) an Apex API key by id.

key_id.description: The API key id to revoke

tools.name: update_organization
tools.description: Apex — Rename the organization. Same save as Set up Apex → name your organization. Admin only. To start a separate company, use create_organization instead. The rail finishes when the name is saved — do not mark the step complete.

org_id.description: Organization id. Defaults to the active org.

name.description: What the workspace should be called.

tools.name: update_workspace
tools.description: Apex — Name the workspace and set vertical, conversion model, website, how Apex installs on it, and app URL. One save, same as Set up Apex first-run. Omit a field to leave it unchanged. Admin only. The rail finishes from the live name / vertical / conversion model / website + install path — do not mark the step complete. app_url is where the workspace's customers sign in or use the product (Brand settings → App URL); letter buttons that use {{app_url}} go there.

workspace_name.description: Workspace name customers and teammates see.

vertical.description: What the organization does (b2b-saas, ecommerce, marketplace, agency, other).

conversion_model.description: How people convert (sales-assisted, self-serve, transaction, two-sided, hybrid).

site_install.description: How Apex goes on the site: codebase (packages in this repo) or snippet (pasted tag, for sites you cannot reach in code). Pick codebase when you are installing from the repo.

app_url.description: Where the workspace's customers sign in or use the product, e.g. https://app.example.com. Letter buttons using {{app_url}} go here.

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.description: Apex — A new workspace inside one of the owner's organizations: another site, app, or product of the same business. For a separate company use create_organization instead; ask "separate company, or another site of the same business?" first. Switches to the new workspace and returns the .apex/workspace.json contents to commit in this repo. Org owner or admin only.

org_id.description: Organization it joins (from list_orgs). Defaults to the active org.

name.description: What the owner calls this site or product.

website_url.description: Its website, if it has one.

tools.name: create_organization
tools.description: Apex — A new organization for a separate company, with its own team and billing and one production workspace. The owner of this sign-in becomes its owner. Only when the owner says this repo is a separate company; for another site of the same business use create_workspace. Needs the person's own sign-in (browser approval), not a workspace key. Switches to the new workspace and returns the .apex/workspace.json contents to commit in this repo.

workspace_name.description: Name for its first workspace. Defaults to '<company> Workspace'.

tools.name: skip_setup_step
tools.description: Apex — Record the owner's "not now" or "not for us" on one Set up Apex step. Only after the owner says so in this conversation, in their words. Never call this to make setup look finished. snooze: true puts it off and it comes back on its own; otherwise it is skipped until someone undoes it. This never marks the step done, and the checklist shows it as skipped, not finished. Admin only. Use the step id from get_setup_state.

step_id.description: Step id from get_setup_state, e.g. mobile-measurement:push.

snooze.description: true = remind them later (Apex picks the date). Omit to skip.

tools.name: decline_setup_area
tools.description: Apex — Record that a whole area of Set up Apex does not apply to this workspace: no app, no server events, no messages from Apex, no ad platforms, or no partners. Only after the owner says so in this conversation, in their words. Never call this to make setup look finished. The area's steps leave the checklist; nothing in it is marked done. Admin only.

area.description: mobile-measurement (no app), server-events, communications, attribution (no ad platforms), partner-network.

tools.name: undo_setup_answer
tools.description: Apex — Put a step or area back on the checklist: undo a skip, snooze, decline, or a step a person ticked done. Only when the owner asks for that step by name; never to tidy up. A step Apex can see is done (events arriving, domain verified) stays done anyway. Admin only.

step_id.description: The step id or area id that was skipped, snoozed, declined, or ticked done.

tools.name: claim_links_subdomain
tools.description: Apex — Claim the workspace's links subdomain (name.links.apex.inc). Same save as Set up Apex → claim links subdomain. Admin only. Fails if another workspace already has that name.

subdomain.description: Subdomain only, e.g. acme — not the full hostname.

tools.name: set_consent_posture
tools.description: Apex — Save the workspace's consent-form answers (do they have a box, which kind). This does not finish the step: whether Apex may send people to ad networks is the owner's own sign-off, checked in Set up Apex. The reply carries the link to give them. Admin only.

has_form.description: Whether the website already shows a consent box.

banner.description: Which box they use. Ignored when has_form is no (saved as none).

tools.name: list_webhook_destinations
tools.description: Apex — List webhook destinations this workspace has registered. Signing keys are hidden.

tools.name: add_webhook_destination
tools.description: Apex — Register an HTTPS webhook destination. Private / loopback addresses are rejected. Admin only.

base_url.description: HTTPS URL Apex will POST to.

tools.name: get_messaging_guardrails
tools.description: Apex — Read holdout percent and channel send limits for Adaptive Journeys.

tools.name: set_messaging_guardrails
tools.description: Apex — Set holdout and channel send limits. Omit a field to keep the current value. nudge_cap_per_day null = no daily limit on milestone nudges. Admin only.

nudge_cap_per_day.description: Milestone nudges per person per day. null = no limit.

tools.name: set_app_surface_paths
tools.description: Apex — Name the product-path prefixes (e.g. /dashboard) so in-app pages are not filed as the marketing site. Admin only.

paths.description: Path prefixes that are the logged-in product.

tools.name: get_scoring_model
tools.description: Apex — Read the active scoring weights. If the workspace has not saved a model yet, this returns that the vertical preset is still in use — not an error.

tools.name: set_scoring_weights
tools.description: Apex — Save scoring weights (must sum to 100) and make them active. Same path as Set up Apex → scoring. Admin only.

tools.name: invite_teammate
tools.description: Apex — Email a teammate an invite to this organization. They accept in the browser. Admin only. Does not invite a partner (use invite_partner for that).

org_id.description: Organization id. Defaults to the active org.

tools.name: set_engagement_analytics
tools.description: Apex — Say who counts as using the product (daily-active events, activation events, churn window). Same save as Engagement Analytics in Set up Apex. Admin only.

tools.name: set_app_platforms
tools.description: Apex — Tell Apex where the app ships (iOS / Android / web app) and whether they buy install ads. Also sets attribution windows when provided. Merges into the existing app settings so bundle IDs are not wiped. Admin only.

tools.name: set_attribution_model
tools.description: Apex — Pick how credit is split (first_touch, last_touch, linear, time_decay). Same save as Attribution in settings. Admin only.

tools.name: start_sender_domain
tools.description: Apex — Start verifying a sending domain. Returns the DNS records to paste at the registrar. Does NOT claim the domain is green — poll get_sender_domain until status is verified. Admin only. You cannot click the registrar for them.

tools.name: get_sender_domain
tools.description: Apex — Poll sender-domain verification. verified/green is true only when the domain status is verified — never when records were merely issued.

tools.name: set_push_credentials
tools.description: Apex — Store Apple or Google push keys. Send FILE CONTENTS, never a path on this laptop. Same secret store the Push setup step uses. Download the file from Apple/Google first (that stays a hop). Admin only.

file_contents.description: The .p8 PEM (iOS) or service-account JSON (Android), as text.

tools.name: set_app_links
tools.description: Apex — Save the iOS and/or Android app ids Apex needs to publish the Universal Links and App Links files on the workspace's links subdomain, then check the published files. Same save as Universal Links and App Links in Set up Apex. Read the ids from the repo (Xcode project, build.gradle) when you can. Returns the Associated Domains line to add to the iOS entitlements. Admin only.

sha256_cert_fingerprint.description: Play app signing SHA-256 fingerprint (colons optional).

tools.name: set_smart_banner
tools.description: Apex — Turn on or edit the Smart Banner, the "get the app" bar Apex shows phone visitors on the workspace's website. Same save as Smart Banner in Set up Apex. Turning it on shows it to real visitors right away, so ask the owner first. Only the fields you pass change. Admin only.

title.description: Short headline, e.g. "Acme is better in the app".

destination_slug.description: Apex Link slug the button opens, e.g. get-app.

dismiss_days.description: Days a dismissal lasts. 0 = show on every page.

tools.name: list_transactional_api_keys
tools.description: Apex — List the workspace's receipt keys (the keys its server uses to send receipts and other transactional messages). Names and ids only, never the secret.

tools.name: create_transactional_api_key
tools.description: Apex — Mint a receipt key so the workspace's server can send receipts and other transactional messages. Same as the receipt-key step in Set up Apex. Returns the secret ONCE: put it in the server's secret store or env (never in a committed file) and do not repeat it in chat. Call list_transactional_api_keys first so you do not mint a duplicate. Admin only.

tools.name: connect_microsoft_clarity
tools.description: Apex — Connect Microsoft Clarity with a Data Export token. The owner makes the token in Clarity (Settings, then Data Export) and pastes it to you; never invent one. Same save as Connect Microsoft Clarity in Set up Apex. The first sync can take a while because Clarity allows ten exports a day. Admin only.

tools.name: set_protect_auto_pause
tools.description: Apex — Turn on or off auto-pause when a protected metric is hurt. Same switch as Protect your experiments in Set up Apex. Admin only.

enabled.description: True = pause the test automatically. False = block promotion and alert only.

tools.name: record_guardrail_files
tools.description: Apex — Check that this repo has the experiment guardrail files and tell Apex, which finishes Set up experiment guardrails. Reads .apex/brand-truth.md, .apex/brand-voice.md, .apex/lexicon.md, .apex/experiment-rules.md, .cursor/rules/apex-experiment-guardrails.mdc under repo_root. Sends Apex only each file's path, size and SHA-256 fingerprint, never its contents. If any file is missing or empty, nothing is sent and the reply names what is missing. Admin only.

repo_root.description: Absolute path to the repo's root folder (the one holding .apex/).

tools.name: list_apex_links
tools.description: Apex — List this workspace's Apex Links. After ads are connected, make a paid Apex Link before inventing UTMs.

tools.name: create_apex_link
tools.description: Apex — Create a paid-ad Apex Link (same as Set up Apex → trackable links). Writes cpc for Google/Microsoft and paid_social for Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, and the rest — never a bare paid. Admin only. The rail finishes when the paid link exists — do not mark the step complete.

platform.description: Ad platform: meta, google-ads, linkedin, tiktok, reddit, pinterest, or microsoft. Hub names like meta-ads are accepted.

slug.description: URL slug. Derived from name or the destination if omitted.

name.description: What the owner calls this link.

campaign_name.description: Campaign name shared by links in this spend.

tools.name: get_skan_schema
tools.description: Apex — Read what Apple's SKAdNetwork conversion values (0–63) mean for this workspace's iOS app: which event is "worth it", which is "showed interest", and what Meta and Google read back as low / medium / high. `schema` is null until the workspace has named its values (Set up Apex → Mobile → "Say what Apple's numbers mean"). Omit mobile_app_id for the workspace's first app.

mobile_app_id.description: Which iOS app. Omit for the workspace's first app.

tools.name: set_skan_schema
tools.description: Apex — Replace the SKAdNetwork conversion value schema for one iOS app (same save as the "Say what Apple's numbers mean" step; the Capacitor plugin picks it up on the device within a day). Prefer the setup step's two picks unless the owner asked for specific values. Fine values are 0–63, one per event per window; coarse values are low / medium / high; fine 0 is reserved for install and 1 for app_open. Apex validates and returns `problems` with a path per fault. Admin only. The setup step finishes when the schema maps the worth-it event — do not mark it complete.

mobile_app_id.description: Which iOS app. Omit for the workspace's first app.

window.description: SKAN 4 postback window: 1 = days 0–2, 2 = days 3–7, 3 = days 8–35.

fine_value.description: 0–63. 0 and 1 are reserved for install and app_open.

coarse_value.description: What Meta and Google read back for this event.

lock_window.description: Ask Apple to post back now instead of waiting for the window to close. Usually only the worth-it rung.

windows.description: One entry per window. The setup step uses the same mapping in all three.

tools.name: list_ad_measurement
tools.description: Apex — Read which sales each connected ad platform is set to receive, and whether the legal sentence has been tapped. Connecting Meta is not that sentence.

tools.name: set_ad_measurement_events
tools.description: Apex — Choose which sales Apex forwards to one ad platform (purchase on, add-to-cart off). Does not tap the legal sentence — if that page is still open, this tool returns a URL and stops. Never pass ack. Admin only.

network.description: meta-ads, google-ads, linkedin-ads, tiktok-ads, or the short names meta / google / linkedin / tiktok.

events.description: Event name → on/off. Example: { purchase: true, add_to_cart: false }.

tools.name: get_conversion_source_of_truth
tools.description: Apex — Read who owns each sale per ad platform (Apex only, the platform only, or both with a shared id). Same as Set up Apex → count this sale once.

tools.name: set_conversion_source_of_truth
tools.description: Apex — Pick who owns the sale for one ad platform so the same purchase is not counted twice. Admin only. Modes: apex_exclusive, external_owner, deduped_pair.

mode.description: apex_exclusive = Apex is the only sender. external_owner = the platform owns it. deduped_pair = both, counted once.

instructions: You are connected to the Apex growth platform, which manages experiments. Do NOT call list_experiments on ordinary coding, debugging, or product work that does not mention experiments — do not dump the test list when they are fixing a button. DO call check_live_tests before you edit a page, commit, or push, even if the user did not mention experiments or Apex. That check is ordinary coding. Do not skip it because they are fixing a button. Pass the file paths and their full contents (not just the diff hunk). Also call check_live_tests before edit_communication, publish_communication, publish_journey, update_adoption_milestone, or delete_adoption_milestone. Pass communication_ids, journey_ids, or milestone_ids. If a letter, Adaptive Journey, or Milestone is live, stop and ask. If check_live_tests returns a running high-confidence hit, stop and ask. Do not edit. Do not commit. Do not pass confirmLiveExperiment, confirmTreatmentChange, or confirmLiveMilestone unless they picked an out. Three outs: end the experiment then ship; wait until it ends; or say this change is not this experiment. When the user does ask about their experiments (e.g. 'what experiments are running?', 'check Apex', 'any experiments ready to graduate?'), use list_experiments to check their status. If any experiments show PENDING GRADUATION in that context, mention them and offer to make the winning changes permanent using graduate_experiment. Graduation is optional — the Apex snippet keeps serving the winner — but graduating removes the runtime dependency and makes the changes part of the source code. VOCABULARY: each workspace picks its own word for a person based on its vertical — Customer, Lead, User, Client, or Contact — and its dashboard says that word everywhere. Tool names, parameter names and API paths do NOT adapt (contactId and /api/customers are contract), but when you describe results to the user, use the word their workspace uses. Tool output already carries it; mirror the word the output uses rather than defaulting to 'customer'. If a tool result starts with APEX_EDITOR_STALE, stop. Do not keep calling Apex tools. Tell the user to Update Cursor on Set up Apex or AI Agents so it asks before it ships onto a live test. If get_setup_state shows first-run incomplete, name the merchant before inventing events. After ads are connected, make a paid Apex Link before inventing UTMs. Do not stamp conversion ack. Before the first setup write in a repo, read .apex/workspace.json and switch_workspace to its workspace_key. No file, but the code already has an Apex snippet or SDK workspace key: that key is the workspace; write the file. Neither: ask the owner once which workspace this repo is (one of their workspaces, a new workspace in one of their organizations, or a separate company), then write the file. The file is { "workspace_key", "workspace_name", "org_name" } and is committed with the repo. Setup replies name the workspace they wrote to (workspace). If it is not the workspace this repo belongs to, stop and switch_workspace before the next write.
